newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan industrial group to visit China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan industrial group to visit China.

text.p: A Taiwan industry umbrella group is expected to send a delegation to rival China later this month, officials said on Tuesday.
"We plan to send a group to northeastern China on May 13 to understand the needs of our businessmen there," a spokeswoman for Taiwan's Chinese National Federation of Industries said by telephone.
She said the delegation, including some 10 senior federation board members, would visit Dalian, Shenyang and other northeastern Chinese cities.
The local United Evening News reported that officials from the Board of Foreign Trade would also join the group.
Both the spokeswoman and board officials declined to comment on the newspaper report.

Taiwan, separated from China at the end of a civil war in 1949, bans direct contact and investment on the mainland. All investment must be government approved and routed through Hong Kong or other third places.
Some 30,000 companies from Taiwan, which China regards as a renegade province, have poured more than US$30 billion into the mainland.
Due to strained ties, Taiwan has expressed concern that its economy may become too dependent on China.
In April, President Lee Teng-hui said the government would remain cautious on investment policy toward its giant neighbour.
Economics Minister Wang Chih-kang last week told parliament the government had drafted a set of criteria to govern local investment in China.
